statements.text: # Patient survey — medication refills (summary, 412 responses)

- 58% have run out of a long-term medication at least once in the past year. - The most common reason (71%) was forgetting to request a renewal in time. - 64% would like a reminder; the most requested lead time was one week. - 39% have a family member who helps manage their medications. - 22% said small text in the current app is a problem. - Free-text comments asked for a way to see whether a renewal request had been received and whether the pharmacy had the medication ready.

# FHIR API gateway — endpoints available to the patient app

- `GET /MedicationRequest?patient={id}&status=active` returns the patient's active prescriptions, including `dispenseRequest.quantity`, `dispenseRequest.expectedSupplyDuration` and `dispenseRequest.numberOfRepeatsAllowed`. - `POST /Task` with code `renewal-request` and `focus` = the MedicationRequest creates a renewal request in the EHR renewal queue. - Fill status arrives as `MedicationDispense` resources with `status=completed` when the pharmacy has dispensed. - Authentication: OAuth 2.0 with SMART on FHIR patient scopes (`patient/MedicationRequest.read`, `patient/Task.write`). A proxy (caregiver) token carries the patient's id and the proxy's own identity. - Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per user. - Every call is logged by the gateway as a FHIR AuditEvent.
# Patient portal proxy access policy (excerpt) — PP-3

1. An adult patient may grant proxy access to another adult by recording consent in the portal or app. 2. The consent record must state who the proxy is, what they may do, and when consent was given. 3. The patient may revoke proxy access at any time; revocation takes effect immediately. 4. A proxy acts under their own login and never with the patient's credentials. 5. Every action a proxy takes is recorded against the proxy's identity. 6. Proxy access for patients aged 13-17 requires review by the health information management team.
